4	Authors: The AlgebraicJacobian Contributors

6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0ChartVMonotone
7	import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Sites.LocallyBijective
8	
9	/-!
10	# The two seam antecedents COLLAPSE at a one-chart atlas: the pair forces an ISOMORPHISM
11	
12	Four rows and three file headers in this project defer to one question, in these words:
13	**"inhabitation of the pair `(huniv V, hcov V)` is unmeasured at every `V` and may be empty
14	everywhere"** (`AJCR.w4-rep.datum.chart-restrict`, repeated verbatim on
15	`…datum.atlas-coupling`, whose own summary adds that its round "removed a candidate escape from
16	that question, it did not answer it").  Five files of endpoint refutations and monotonicity
17	results (`Pic0ChartRestrictedFibreSat`, `Pic0ChartVMonotone`, `Pic0ChartBotRefute`,
18	`Pic0ChartAtlasCoupling`, `Pic0ChartCoverForcesNonInj`) all stop there.
19	
20	**This file answers what the pair IS.**  For a one-chart atlas the two antecedents are not two
21	independent conditions to be met at some lucky `V` — together they say the chart map is an
22	**isomorphism of sheaves onto `pic0SigmaSheaf C`**, and conversely any such isomorphism
23	satisfies both.  So the question "is the pair inhabited at some `V`?" is *equivalent* to
24	"is `pic0SigmaFunctor C` representable by an open of the divisor scheme?", which is the
25	project's own headline restricted to a one-chart atlas.
26	
27	## Why this is a collapse and not a restatement
28	
29	The two clauses are `MorphismProperty.relative`-shaped and sieve-shaped respectively, and
30	nothing in the tree related them.  The bridge is that each is *half of a bijectivity*:
31	
32	* antecedent 1 (`IsChartUniv`, i.e. `IsOpenImmersion.presheaf`) **implies** elementwise
33	  injectivity on every test — that is `injective_of_isOpenImmersion_presheaf`
34	  (`Pic0ChartOpenImmersionCriterion.lean`), which routes through
35	  `IsOpenImmersion.le_monomorphisms`.  Injectivity on the nose is *stronger* than
36	  `Presheaf.IsLocallyInjective`, so it gives it (`isLocallyInjective_of_injective`);
37	* antecedent 2 is `Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective` verbatim;
38	* and mathlib's `Sheaf.isLocallyBijective_iff_isIso` turns locally-injective-plus-locally-
39	  surjective into `IsIso` — **provided both sides are sheaves**.  The target is one by
40	  construction (`pic0SigmaFunctor_isSheaf`); the source is one because the big Zariski topology
41	  is **subcanonical** (`AlgebraicGeometry.subcanonical_zariskiTopology`, mathlib), so `yoneda.obj X`
42	  is a sheaf for it with no hypothesis on `X` at all.
43	
44	That last point is the step that had never been taken here: the chart source is representable,
45	and on a subcanonical site a representable presheaf is a sheaf, so the seam's two antecedents
46	live in a category where mathlib's bijectivity criterion applies.  Nothing about `pic⁰`,
47	divisors, charts or the curve enters any proof below.
48	
49	## What this buys, stated as three consequences and one non-consequence
50	
51	* **`chartIso_of_seam`** — the collapse. Both antecedents at a one-chart atlas give
52	  `IsIso` of the sheaf morphism.
53	* **`representableBy_of_seam`** — hence `pic0SigmaFunctor C` is represented by the chart
54	  source *on the nose*, without going through mathlib's 01JJ gluing engine at all.  For a
55	  one-chart atlas the whole `Scheme.LocalRepresentability` apparatus of
56	  `pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` is bypassed: the glued scheme is the chart.
57	* **`exists_retraction_of_seam`** — the sharp constraint on `V`.  If the pair holds at `V` then
58	  the open inclusion `V.ι : ↥V ⟶ D.left` is a **split mono in `Scheme`**: the chart map
59	  composed with the inverse retracts it.  So a working `V` is not merely a proper intermediate
60	  open (which is all the endpoint results gave); it is a **retract of the divisor scheme**.
61	  That is a much stronger structural demand, and it is the form in which the inhabitation
62	  question should be attacked next.
63	* **The non-consequence, and it is why this file does not claim to have answered the question.**
64	  `IsIso` is an *equivalent reformulation*, not a refutation and not a witness.  Nothing below
65	  exhibits a `V` at which the pair holds, and nothing below refutes one.  What changes is that
66	  the target is now a single familiar statement about one morphism instead of a conjunction of
67	  two conditions of different shapes — and that the retraction constraint is available to
68	  whoever attacks it.
69	
70	## Scope: one chart, and that is a real restriction
71	
72	Every statement here is for a **`PUnit`-indexed** atlas.  That is not a convenience: for a
73	general `ι` the two antecedents are about *different* morphisms (`f i` versus `Sigma.desc f`),
74	`Sigma.desc f` is not a map out of a representable, and the collapse genuinely fails to
75	typecheck.  The one-chart case is not a caricature either — `Pic0AtlasFromDivRep.lean` builds a
76	one-chart atlas, and `IsChartUniv`, `RestrictedChartFibre` and `restrictedChartFibre_top_iff`
77	are all stated for one.  But a lane must not read `chartIso_of_seam` as a statement about
78	`mixedParamChart` at arbitrary `ι`.  `isLocallySurjective_oneChart` below is the bridge that
79	makes the one-chart hypothesis usable in the coproduct spelling the seam consumes, so the
80	restriction is to the *index*, not to the *spelling*.
81	
82	## Main declarations
83	
84	* `AlgebraicGeometry.chartSourceSheaf` — the chart source as a sheaf, by subcanonicity.
85	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isLocallySurjective_oneChart` — antecedent 2 in the coproduct spelling
86	  gives local surjectivity of the single chart.
87	* `AlgebraicGeometry.chartIso_of_seam` — **the collapse**.
88	* `AlgebraicGeometry.seam_of_chartIso` — **the converse**, so this is an equivalence and not a
89	  weakening.
90	* `AlgebraicGeometry.representableBy_of_seam` — the representation, engine-free.
91	* `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_retraction_of_seam` — `V.ι` is a split mono.
92	-/
93	
94	set_option autoImplicit false
95	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
96	
97	universe u
98	
99	open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite
100	
101	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
102	
103	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
104	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
105	variable [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] [GeometricallyReduced C.hom]
106	
107	noncomputable section
108	
109	/-! ## The chart source is a sheaf -/
110	
111	/-- **A representable presheaf is a big-Zariski sheaf**, because the big Zariski topology is
112	subcanonical (`subcanonical_zariskiTopology`, mathlib).
113	
114	Recorded as a named lemma because it is the step the whole file rests on and the step nobody
115	had taken: the chart source of the atlas is `yoneda.obj (V : Scheme)`, hence a sheaf, hence the
116	chart map is a morphism *of sheaves* — which is what lets mathlib's bijectivity criterion see
117	it.  No hypothesis on the scheme. -/
118	theorem isSheaf_yoneda_obj (X : Scheme.{u}) :
119	    Presheaf.IsSheaf Scheme.zariskiTopology (yoneda.obj X) :=
120	  (isSheaf_iff_isSheaf_of_type _ _).mpr
121	    (GrothendieckTopology.Subcanonical.isSheaf_of_isRepresentable (yoneda.obj X))
122	
123	/-- The chart source bundled as a sheaf on the big Zariski site. -/
124	def chartSourceSheaf (X : Scheme.{u}) : Sheaf Scheme.zariskiTopology.{u} (Type u) :=
125	  ⟨yoneda.obj X, isSheaf_yoneda_obj X⟩
126	
127	variable (C) in
128	/-- A chart map read as a morphism of sheaves. -/
129	def chartSheafHom {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : yoneda.obj X ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1) :
130	    chartSourceSheaf X ⟶ pic0SigmaSheaf C :=
131	  ⟨f⟩
132	
133	/-! ## Antecedent 2 at a one-chart atlas -/
134	
135	variable (C) in
136	/-- **Antecedent 2, de-coproducted at one chart**: local surjectivity of `Sigma.desc` for a
137	`PUnit`-indexed family gives local surjectivity of the chart itself.
138	
139	The image sieve of `Sigma.desc` is contained in that of the single chart, because a section of
140	the coproduct presheaf resolves into a section of the one summand
141	(`FunctorToTypes.jointly_surjective'`, the lemma `Pic0ChartBotRefute.lean` first brought into
142	this project) and `Sigma.ι_desc` identifies the two readings.
143	
144	This is what makes the one-chart restriction a restriction on the *index* only: a lane holding
145	the instance the seam consumes holds this. -/
146	theorem isLocallySurjective_oneChart {X : Scheme.{u}}
147	    (f : yoneda.obj X ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
148	    (h : Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology
149	      (Sigma.desc (fun _ : PUnit.{u+1} => f))) :
150	    Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology f := by
151	  haveI := h
152	  constructor
153	  intro T s
154	  refine Scheme.zariskiTopology.superset_covering ?_
155	    (Presheaf.imageSieve_mem (J := Scheme.zariskiTopology)
156	      (Sigma.desc (fun _ : PUnit.{u+1} => f)) s)
157	  intro Y g hg
158	  obtain ⟨t, ht⟩ := hg
159	  obtain ⟨i, y, rfl⟩ := CategoryTheory.FunctorToTypes.jointly_surjective'
160	    (Discrete.functor fun _ : PUnit.{u+1} => yoneda.obj X) (op Y) t
161	  refine ⟨y, ?_⟩
162	  rw [← ht, ← NatTrans.comp_app_apply]
163	  simpa using
164	    (NatTrans.congr_app (Sigma.ι_desc (fun _ : PUnit.{u+1} => f) i.as) (op Y)).symm ▸ rfl
165	
166	/-! ## The collapse -/
167	
168	variable (C) in
169	/-- **THE COLLAPSE**: at a one-chart atlas the two seam antecedents together say the chart map
170	is an isomorphism onto the Σ-sheaf.
171	
172	Antecedent 1 gives injectivity on every test, hence local injectivity; antecedent 2 is local
173	surjectivity; and on a site where both sides are sheaves mathlib's
174	`Sheaf.isLocallyBijective_iff_isIso` closes it.  The source is a sheaf by subcanonicity
175	(`isSheaf_yoneda_obj`) — the observation this file exists to spend.
176	
177	Read against the five files of `V`-interval results: those establish that a working `V` must be
178	a proper intermediate open.  This says what a working `V` *is*. -/
179	theorem chartIso_of_seam {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : yoneda.obj X ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
180	    (hf : IsOpenImmersion.presheaf f)
181	    (hcov : Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology f) :
182	    IsIso (chartSheafHom C f) := by
183	  haveI : Presheaf.IsLocallyInjective Scheme.zariskiTopology (chartSheafHom C f).hom :=
184	    Presheaf.isLocallyInjective_of_injective _ _
185	      (fun T => injective_of_isOpenImmersion_presheaf hf T)
186	  haveI : Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology (chartSheafHom C f).hom := hcov
187	  exact (Sheaf.isLocallyBijective_iff_isIso (chartSheafHom C f)).mp
188	    ⟨inferInstance, inferInstance⟩
189	
190	variable (C) in
191	/-- **THE CONVERSE**, so the collapse is an equivalence and not a weakening (the `I-0896`
192	criterion).  An isomorphism satisfies both antecedents:
193	
194	* antecedent 1 because `IsOpenImmersion.presheaf` is `MorphismProperty.relative`, which
195	  contains the isomorphisms (`MorphismProperty.of_isIso`, available since `relative` is
196	  multiplicative and respects isos);
197	* antecedent 2 because a locally surjective map is what an iso trivially is
198	  (`Presheaf.isLocallySurjective_of_iso`).
199	
200	Together with `chartIso_of_seam` this says: **the pair is inhabited at `V` if and only if the
201	restricted chart is an isomorphism of sheaves.**  So the unmeasured inhabitation question has
202	not been weakened into something easier — it has been identified. -/
203	theorem seam_of_chartIso {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : yoneda.obj X ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
204	    (h : IsIso f) :
205	    IsOpenImmersion.presheaf f
206	      ∧ Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology f := by
207	  haveI := h
208	  exact ⟨MorphismProperty.of_isIso (P := IsOpenImmersion.presheaf) f, inferInstance⟩
209	
210	/-! ## The representation, without the gluing engine -/
211	
212	variable (C) in
213	/-- **The seam's conclusion at a one-chart atlas, engine-free**: the two antecedents represent
214	`pic0SigmaFunctor C` by the chart source itself.
215	
216	`pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` obtains its representing object from mathlib's 01JJ
217	`Scheme.LocalRepresentability` gluing engine, as
218	`(Scheme.LocalRepresentability.glueData hf).glued`.  At one chart that is unnecessary: the
219	underlying presheaf map of the iso is already an equivalence at every test, and naturality is
220	the chart map's own naturality.  So a lane that closes the pair at one `V` does not owe the
221	glue-data bookkeeping — it gets the representation directly, over the chart.
222	
223	This is stated for `pic0SigmaFunctor` rather than `pic0TypeFunctor`: the Σ-descent to the
224	slice is `Functor.RepresentableBy.overSlice`, exactly as in `pic0RepresentableByOfCharts`, and
225	is not re-proved here. -/
226	def representableBy_of_seam {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : yoneda.obj X ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
227	    (hf : IsOpenImmersion.presheaf f)
228	    (hcov : Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology f) :
229	    (pic0SigmaFunctor C).RepresentableBy X :=
230	  letI : IsIso f := by
231	    haveI := chartIso_of_seam C f hf hcov
232	    exact (inferInstance : IsIso ((sheafToPresheaf Scheme.zariskiTopology (Type u)).map
233	      (chartSheafHom C f)))
234	  { homEquiv := fun {T} => Iso.toEquiv ((asIso f).app (op T))
235	    homEquiv_comp := fun {_T _T'} g x => NatTrans.naturality_apply f g.op x }
236	
237	/-! ## The sharp constraint on `V` -/
238	
239	variable (C) in
240	/-- **A WORKING `V` IS A RETRACT OF THE CHART SOURCE.**
241	
242	If the two antecedents hold for `restrictChart f V` then `V.ι : ↥V ⟶ X` is a **split mono in
243	`Scheme`**: its retraction is `yoneda.preimage (f ≫ inv (restrictChart f V))`, i.e. "read the
244	class, then invert the restricted chart".  Yoneda is full, so this is an honest morphism of
245	schemes and not merely a presheaf-level section.
246	
247	This strictly strengthens what the endpoint literature gives.  `Pic0ChartRestrictedFibreSat`
248	and `Pic0ChartVMonotone` establish that a working `V` must be a *proper intermediate open*;
249	this says it must be a *retract*, which for an open subscheme is a strong structural demand
250	(e.g. it forces `V.ι` to be a topological embedding admitting a continuous left inverse on all
251	of `X`, so `V` meets every connected component and its closure is `X` whenever `X` is
252	irreducible and `V` nonempty).
253	
254	Deliberately not pushed to a refutation.  Whether the divisor scheme admits a proper open
255	retract is a question about `DivScheme`'s geometry that this file does not touch, and asserting
256	it cannot is exactly the kind of unverified claim the `unverified-counterexample-in-docstring`
257	lesson is about.  What is established is the obligation's *shape*. -/
258	theorem exists_retraction_of_seam {X : Scheme.{u}}
259	    (f : yoneda.obj X ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1) (V : X.Opens)
260	    (hf : IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (restrictChart f V))
261	    (hcov : Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology (restrictChart f V)) :
262	    ∃ r : X ⟶ (V : Scheme.{u}), V.ι ≫ r = 𝟙 _ := by
263	  letI : IsIso (restrictChart f V) := by
264	    haveI := chartIso_of_seam C (restrictChart f V) hf hcov
265	    exact (inferInstance : IsIso ((sheafToPresheaf Scheme.zariskiTopology (Type u)).map
266	      (chartSheafHom C (restrictChart f V))))
267	  refine ⟨yoneda.preimage (f ≫ inv (restrictChart f V)), ?_⟩
268	  apply yoneda.map_injective
269	  have h1 : yoneda.map (V.ι ≫ yoneda.preimage (f ≫ inv (restrictChart f V)))
270	      = yoneda.map V.ι ≫ (f ≫ inv (restrictChart f V)) := by
271	    rw [Functor.map_comp, yoneda.map_preimage]
272	  have h2 : yoneda.map V.ι ≫ (f ≫ inv (restrictChart f V))
273	      = 𝟙 (yoneda.obj (V : Scheme.{u})) := by
274	    rw [← Category.assoc]; exact IsIso.hom_inv_id (restrictChart f V)
275	  rw [h1, h2, ← yoneda.map_id]
276	
277	/-! ## The retraction collapses the interval on a DENSE open
278	
279	The retraction above is a statement about an arbitrary open.  On a *dense* one it forces
280	`V = ⊤`, which sends the seam back to the endpoint literature's `⊤` case — and that case is
281	refuted the moment the Abel chart fails to be injective.  So on the geometrically natural
282	candidates for `V` the interval has no interior at all. -/
283	
284	/-- **A dense working `V` in a reduced separated ambient scheme is `⊤`.**
285	
286	The retraction `r` is a *left* inverse of `V.ι`; to promote it to a two-sided one we need
287	`r ≫ V.ι = 𝟙 X`, and that follows from mathlib's agreement principle
288	`ext_of_isDominant`: the two morphisms `r ≫ V.ι` and `𝟙 X` agree after precomposition with
289	the dominant `V.ι`, and `X` is reduced and separated.  An iso open inclusion is surjective on
290	points, hence `V = ⊤`.
291	
292	`IsDominant V.ι` is exactly density of `V` (mathlib's `IsDominant` is denseness of the range),
293	and for an *irreducible* ambient scheme every nonempty open is dense — which is the case the
294	divisor scheme is expected to be in.  So this is not an exotic side condition: on an
295	irreducible reduced separated chart source, **every nonempty working `V` is `⊤`**.
296	
297	The hypotheses `[IsReduced X]`, `[X.IsSeparated]`, `[IsDominant V.ι]` are all load-bearing and
298	none is about `pic⁰`: this is a general fact about split-mono open immersions. -/
299	theorem eq_top_of_retraction_of_isDominant {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsReduced X] [X.IsSeparated]
300	    (V : X.Opens) [IsDominant (V.ι)]
301	    (r : X ⟶ (V : Scheme.{u})) (hr : V.ι ≫ r = 𝟙 _) :
302	    V = ⊤ := by
303	  haveI : IsIso (V.ι) := by
304	    refine ⟨r, hr, ?_⟩
305	    refine ext_of_isDominant (X := X) (Y := X) (W := (V : Scheme.{u})) (V.ι) ?_
306	    rw [← Category.assoc, hr, Category.id_comp, Category.comp_id]
307	  have hsurj : Function.Surjective (V.ι).base :=
308	    (TopCat.homeoOfIso (asIso (Scheme.forgetToTop.map (V.ι)))).surjective
309	  refine top_le_iff.mp fun x _ => ?_
310	  obtain ⟨y, rfl⟩ := hsurj x
311	  exact y.2
312	
313	variable (C) in
314	/-- **THE INTERVAL HAS NO INTERIOR ON DENSE OPENS**: the two antecedents at a dense `V` force
315	`V = ⊤`.
316	
317	Composite of `exists_retraction_of_seam` with `eq_top_of_retraction_of_isDominant`.  This is
318	the statement to read against the four rows that call the inhabitation question open: they are
319	right that it is open, and this says **where** it can be open.  Every candidate `V` that is
320	dense in the chart source — which, on an irreducible chart source, means every nonempty
321	candidate — is `⊤`.  And `⊤` is refuted by
322	`not_restrictedChartFibre_top_of_not_injective` (`Pic0ChartRestrictedFibreSat.lean`, downstream
323	of this file so the name does not resolve here) as soon as the Abel chart fails to be injective
324	on one test — the `abel-noninj` fork.
325	
326	**What this does NOT prove, stated because the temptation is exactly the error this project has
327	made before** (`two-refutations-are-not-inhabitation`).  It does not refute the pair.  Two
328	things stand between this and a refutation, and neither is supplied here: the chart source must
329	be shown irreducible (or the candidate `V` shown dense), and the `abel-noninj` fork must be
330	decided in the negative — which three file headers assert and no declaration proves.  What is
331	established is that a lane hunting for a working `V` in the interior of the interval must
332	either exhibit a **non-dense** one or first settle the fork. That is a genuine narrowing of the
333	search, not a closure of it. -/
334	theorem eq_top_of_seam_of_isDominant {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsReduced X] [X.IsSeparated]
335	    (f : yoneda.obj X ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1) (V : X.Opens) [IsDominant (V.ι)]
336	    (hf : IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (restrictChart f V))
337	    (hcov : Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology (restrictChart f V)) :
338	    V = ⊤ := by
339	  obtain ⟨r, hr⟩ := exists_retraction_of_seam C f V hf hcov
340	  exact eq_top_of_retraction_of_isDominant V r hr
341	
342	end
343	
344	end AlgebraicGeometry

name: project-git
description: How git works in an Archon Horizon workspace — one out-of-tree workspace ledger (no per-project repos); read a project's history by pathspec or by a session's commit trailers.
---

Read this before running `git diff`/`git log` on a project.

## The model

- **One out-of-tree workspace ledger.** Archon commits to a single repo whose git
  dir is `.archon-horizon/vcs/workspace.git` with the workspace **root** as its
  work tree (driven via `--git-dir`/`--work-tree`). `<root>/.git` is deliberately
  untouched — it is reserved for a user repo. The ledger records one commit per
  completed session: `config.yaml`, the session's scoped project files, and
  `.archon-horizon/` shared state; never the binary git dirs under
  `.archon-horizon/vcs/`, locks, or other volatile internals.
- **There are no per-project repositories.** A project directory has no nested
  `.git/`, and there is no `.archon-horizon/vcs/<project>.git`. A project's
  "history" is simply the workspace ledger filtered to that project's path.
- **You record your own work by committing to the ledger** with plain `git` (see
  below). Commit after each independently useful, verified proof/file/tooling
  change, before a long build or delegated review, and before expanding scope.
  A multi-hour implementation session should normally have several commits; one
  commit is appropriate only when the work is genuinely atomic. The message +
  diff is how progress is read, so use a semantic, math-first subject. Provenance
  trailers are added automatically; do not write them.

So a plain `git diff` at the root sees only a user repo (if any), never Archon's.
Drive the out-of-tree workspace ledger explicitly (or use `hgit`).

## Recording your work (committing)

Commits go to the ledger, **not** to `<root>/.git` and **not** via any project
`.git` (there is none). Do **not** `export GIT_DIR` / `GIT_WORK_TREE` yourself — that
would redirect `lake` and other tooling. Two equivalent ways to commit:

```bash
# 1) The `hgit` wrapper (on the session env as $HORIZON_GIT) — plain git, ledger-scoped:
"$HORIZON_GIT" add path/to/File.lean
"$HORIZON_GIT" commit -m "feat(chapter): prove foo_lemma" \
  --trailer 'Summary=**Proof.** Closed the compactness step using $K \subseteq X$.'

# 2) The explicit form (identical effect):
git --git-dir="$HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR" --work-tree="$HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE" \
    add path/to/File.lean
git --git-dir="$HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR" --work-tree="$HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE" \
    commit -m "feat(chapter): prove foo_lemma" \
    --trailer 'Summary=**Proof.** Closed the compactness step using $K \subseteq X$.'
```

Ordinary git: the ledger's index tracks HEAD, so `add` then `commit` records your
files on top of it. Horizon's own commits stage in a private index and never leave
anything staged in your way.

- **Prefer the pathspec commit** — name the paths on the commit itself:
  `"$HORIZON_GIT" commit -m "…" --trailer 'Summary=…' -- path/to/File.lean`
  It records exactly those files, ignores whatever else may be staged, and git
  builds its tree from the **current** HEAD — so it cannot silently revert a
  concurrent session's files the way a commit built on a stale index can.
- Add at least one **`Summary` trailer** explaining the important change, not
  merely repeating the subject. Use one trailer per distinct explanation when
  useful. Its value supports Markdown and LaTeX, so concise mathematical context
  such as `--trailer 'Summary=**Invariant.** Preserves $f(x)=x$ on $A$.'` renders
  directly in the dashboard commit item. Keep each trailer on one line; repeat
  `--trailer 'Summary=…'` for a few separate points.
- Do not wait for the whole task to be complete. A checkpoint commit must build
  or otherwise be internally coherent, but it may explicitly leave the next
  named obligation open.
- Stage **explicit paths** you changed rather than `add -A` — the work tree is the
  whole workspace, so `-A` can sweep in unrelated files.
- `Archon-Run`/`Session`/`Role`/`Task`/`Projects` trailers are stamped for you by a
  hook from the session env; your message stays clean.
- Build artifacts (`.lake`, `*.olean`, …) are excluded automatically, and any
  high-confidence credential is **redacted to `XXXX`** in the staged content (not
  blocked), so a broad add still won't leak a secret into the ledger.
- If the guard reports *"redacted possible secret(s) to XXXX"*, it scrubbed a
  matched credential and let the commit through — **rotate the real credential**,
  and check you didn't stage more than you meant to (`ARCHON_HORIZON_ALLOW_SECRETS=1`
  skips the scan entirely). A *separate* guard still **blocks** a commit that would
  silently delete tracked files you didn't change (a stale-index clobber); re-seed
  the index (`git read-tree HEAD && git add -- <your files>`) rather than forcing it.

Then verify **in the ledger**, and verify the **paths**, not just the SHA — a bare
`git cat-file` runs against `<root>/.git`, which has not seen your commit yet and will
make a perfectly real SHA look fabricated:

```bash
"$HORIZON_GIT" ls-tree --name-only HEAD -- path/to/File.lean   # empty ⇒ NOT in HEAD
```

## Concurrent sessions and the clobber guard

Several sessions may commit to the ledger at once. A commit whose index was
seeded from an older HEAD (e.g. `read-tree`, then a concurrent session commits,
then you commit) produces a tree that *lacks* the other session's new files —
plain git would commit it without any error and silently delete their work.
The ledger's `pre-commit` guard now rejects any commit that stages deletions
you did not ask for:

- *"this commit would DELETE N tracked file(s) you did not change"* — your
  index base is stale (or you are committing through a polluted shared index).
  **Do not override.** Re-seed and retry; your own edits are safe in the
  working tree, which concurrent commits never touch:

  ```bash
  "$HORIZON_GIT" read-tree HEAD
  "$HORIZON_GIT" add -- <your files>
  "$HORIZON_GIT" commit -m "…"          # or just: commit -m "…" -- <your files>
  ```

- Deleting a file **on purpose** (moved/retired): set
  `ARCHON_HORIZON_ALLOW_DELETIONS=1` for that one commit.

At the **end of the session**, re-verify content — not just that HEAD moved —
since a stale-based commit elsewhere could have landed after yours (the guard
blocks new offenders, but belt-and-braces):

```bash
"$HORIZON_GIT" cat-file -e HEAD:path/to/File.lean && \
"$HORIZON_GIT" show HEAD:path/to/File.lean | diff -q - path/to/File.lean
```

If you were clobbered anyway: `read-tree HEAD`, re-add your files from the
working tree, commit once.

## Reading history / a project's diff

Run from the workspace root:

```bash
GD=.archon-horizon/vcs/workspace.git

git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. log  --oneline -n 20                       # whole ledger
git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. log  --oneline -n 20 -- <project-path>     # one project
git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. diff HEAD~1 -- <project-path>
git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. diff HEAD~1 -- '<project-path>/*.lean'
git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. show <sha>
```

Each commit carries provenance trailers — `Archon-Run`, `Archon-Session`,
`Archon-Role`, `Archon-Task`, `Archon-Projects` — so you can map a commit to the
run/session that made it and see what it touched without parsing prose:

```bash
git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. \
  log --format='%H %(trailers:key=Archon-Session,valueonly)' -- <project-path>
```

To see what the previous Horizon agent changed, find its session's commit(s) by
the `Archon-Session` trailer and diff each against **its own parent** (what that
commit changed).

## Caveats

- With parallel runs the ledger is one shared branch: commits from several runs
  interleave, and a commit's parent may belong to another run or a dashboard
  publish. Diff a commit against its own parent (what *that* commit changed), not
  across a span of sessions — that would fold in unrelated runs' changes.
- The bundled author identity is `Archon Horizon <archon-horizon@local>`.

objective: 'You are prover lane `ajcr-p4` on Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild.
  This round the objective is deliberately FREE: nobody has told you which declaration
  to prove. Your objective is to identify the FOURTH most important open item standing
  between this project and Picard/Pic^0 representability, claim it publicly, and discharge
  it.


  READ FIRST: protection item `I-0838`. It is the claim protocol for this round''s
  ten parallel lanes and it is not optional — steps 2 through 5 (check ownership,
  claim with `roadmap set --owner ajcr-p4`, announce, release on exit) are what stop
  four lanes proving the same lemma. Also read `I-0491` and `I-0492`, the two binding
  human decisions, before touching the seam.


  YOUR RANK. You take the FOURTH most important item. Rank is a tie-break so four
  lanes do not converge on one target, not a fence: if your item turns out to be blocked
  on another lane''s, say so in the inbox and swap. On a contested item you yield
  to p1, p2 or p3, then take the next.


  YOUR PEERS this round are ajcr-p1, ajcr-p2, ajcr-p3, ajcr-p4 plus the reviewer `review-ajcr`.
  The reviewer is auditing route and organisation and will be correcting the board
  in its first hour — read its inbox items before you fix your target, and re-read
  them if you are about to start something large. It may direct-message you a proposal;
  weigh it against what you hold, and take it if it is genuinely worth more. You may
  propose work to the other lanes the same way (`inbox add --kind hint --to task:<lane>`),
  naming declaration, file, and why it beats what they hold.


  HOW TO CHOOSE, since this is the part I am delegating to you. "Most important" means:
  measured against the project''s representability headline, what does discharging
  this buy? A leaf that unblocks three others beats a leaf that is merely nearest.
  A leaf whose stated prerequisite turns out to already exist in the file beats both
  — earlier sessions'' costings in this workspace have been wrong in that direction
  more than once, so read the actual Lean hypothesis, not the prose about it. Use
  `horizon graph -p Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild frontier` for the ranked
  view, `horizon roadmap list --focus AJCR.w4-rep` for the board, and `horizon search`
  (which spans both projects AND mathlib) before you prove anything — the premise
  you need is often already next door under a name you would not have grepped.


  THE BAR, and it is higher than usual this round. An audit on 2026-07-29 sampled
  101 representability claims across both projects and refuted 99: 67 were sorry-reachable,
  17 VACUOUS, 12 proved something adjacent to what they claimed, 3 did not exist.
  So:

  - Sorry-free is necessary, not sufficient. Before you report a gate closed, exhibit
  a witness for EVERY antecedent, or state plainly which antecedent remains undischarged.
  "The implication is proved" and "the conclusion holds for some curve" are different
  claims and I want to know which you have.

  - Never introduce a class, structure field, or side condition whose statement does
  not mention the object it is about. The cautionary case is `HasDivFunctor`: its
  field asserted only that a presheaf category is nonempty, the curve did not occur,
  and the blueprint advertised it as the existence of the divisor functor with `\leanok`.
  It survived because nobody read the statement.

  - Never discharge an obligation by projecting the hypothesis you assumed. `choose_spec.1`
  of your own binder is `P → P`.

  - A green build is not evidence of non-vacuity, and `lean_multi_attempt` reports
  every snippet as closing the goal when the file''s imports are stale. Check imports
  before believing a probe.

  - Do not restate an obligation more weakly to make a count go down. If you cannot
  close it, leave it open and say why.


  ONE SHARED LEDGER, ten writers. Another lane''s integrate sweep can commit your
  half-written file before you have measured it once — write risky proofs as explicit
  `sorry` first, measure, then fill. Stage explicit files, never `add -A`. Commit
  at every coherent point; an interrupted lane loses only what was uncommitted. Follow
  the `lean-check` LSP loop for edits and keep `lake build` for the session boundary
  — nine other lanes want the build lock too.


  WHERE THIS PROJECT ACTUALLY STANDS, so you do not rediscover it. AJCR is the architecturally
  sound one. `pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` (`Picard/Pic0SigmaSheaf.lean:161`) and
  `mixedParamRepresentableBy` (`Picard/Pic0ChartAtlasParamFree.lean:125`) are genuinely
  sorry-free and kernel-confirmed on `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]` — honest,
  non-circular implications that WOULD produce a real representing scheme. The problem
  is that all three antecedents are undischarged, with no sorry-free witness for any:
  `IsChartUniv`, Zariski-local surjectivity of `Sigma.desc f`, and `rep i`. A correct
  machine with nothing to feed it.


  That makes your choice unusually concrete: pick whichever of the three missing inputs
  you judge closest, or the leaf that most directly produces one. Do not treat the
  sorry count as the map — the 17 body sorries are 15 in `Challenge.lean` (the statement-only
  headline file, so those ARE the north star, not debt) and 2 in `Pic0ThetaCocycle.lean`.
  The real work is antecedents that no sorry marks.


  The board under `AJCR.w4-rep` (51/74 done) has a deep tail worth reading with suspicion:
  under `datum.dat-d.ddr.certificate`, four siblings are `rejected` (`cert-relocalize`,
  `joint-cover`, `leak-image`, `tube-fibre`) and one is `blocked` (`away-kerspan`).
  Four rejections clustered under one parent usually means the parent''s formulation
  is wrong, not that four different approaches each independently failed. The reviewer
  is determining which; read its finding before you spend a session inside that tail.
  Other open items to weigh: `datum.dat-b` (coverage + injectivity — every pic^0 point
  is hit), `datum.dat-c.c9-chartlocus` and its `chart-u` child (the co-signed chartLocus
  and its openness — the sole gate of dat-b B-6 AND the whole dat-glue), `datum.dat-d.ddr.divrep.u2`
  (the DDR9-U epsilon-identity at the universal point), `datum.dat-glue` (the 01JJ
  RepresentableBy assembly), `datum.dat-j`, `datum.dat-g`, `w4-rep.build-reach` (93
  of 620 modules unrooted, so the axiom probe does not see them — a file nobody imports
  is a file nobody has measured, which may matter to whichever "sorry-free" claim
  you are relying on).


  Costings in this project have been wrong before, in the expensive direction: a handoff
  demanded a new structure field where the localization lemma it asked for was already
  in the file. So for whatever leaf you pick, read its actual Lean hypothesis before
  accepting its stated price. An over-priced leaf is where you win this round.


  The sibling project Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge is readable and `horizon search`
  spans both. It has more Quot/Serre machinery than this project does; if your leaf
  needs cohomological input, look there before building it. Price the consumer''s
  carrier when you do — a cross-project match at object level can be true and irrelevant
  if the cover or instance your statement binds differs.


  WHAT I WANT AT THE END. Your report should answer three things without me having
  to ask: which item you claimed and why it was the fourth-most important, what its
  state is now (closed sorry-free with all antecedents witnessed / closed as an implication
  with named antecedents still open / advanced with the remaining obligation stated

  If your first-choice item collapses on inspection — the prerequisite already exists,
  or the statement turns out vacuous, or another lane got there first — that is a
  finding, not a wasted session. Record it, release the claim, and take the next item.
  Do not sit on a claimed item you are not working.'
